tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__edit_version
tools.description: Publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit (some clients refuse any artifact but your own as owner-only), by replacing text in its current document: use it for a small change instead of sending the whole page to publish_version. The server reads the live index.html, applies every edit in order, and publishes the result as one new version; if any edit cannot be applied, nothing is published. Each old_text must occur exactly once in the document as it stands when that edit is applied: include enough surrounding text to make it unique. base_version must name the live version (from get_artifact, read_artifact, list_files or your last publish result); if it is no longer live the call is rejected with a conflict that names the live version: read what you are changing again and retry. To rename the artifact pass title, which also rewrites the document's <title> element; an edit to that element without title is refused, because the server keeps it in step with the artifact's title. Artifacts that contain a live (collaboratively edited) document cannot be edited here. An artifact made from a type is edited only if this server offers list_files, and only with path: one of its own text files, as list_files lists them, never its page or its type's files.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_files
tools.description: Publish an artifact from files on disk: their bytes go from the files to the artifact and do not pass through you. Prefer this to publish_version when the page's files already exist, when there is more than one file or an image, or when the page is large. For each file give `as`, the path it is served at, and `path`, its absolute path on the machine where your own file tools run; leave `uri` out. index.html is required in a new artifact. Limits for one call: 256 files, 20 MiB a file, 64 MiB in all. The client may refuse a file it will not send, such as a secrets file, a link or a path outside the working folder. Omit slug to create an artifact, private to you. To republish, give slug and base_version (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish); title and icon are kept when omitted. A republish changes only the files named and keeps the rest, which stay served: to take a file away, list it in remove. mode "replace" makes the files named the whole artifact and drops the rest. This tool publishes only to an artifact of yours. **Files Claude did not write**: Claude reads the whole file before publishing it, even when the person asks it not to. Publishing distributes the content, and Claude never distributes what it has not seen. A request for privacy is a reason to read before publishing, not an exemption. If Claude cannot read the file, it does not publish it. **Claude never publishes** a page that impersonates a real person or organization, for example by using their name, branding, byline or domain. Claude also never publishes fabricated records, receipts or reviews presented as genuine, forms or flows that collect credentials or payment details under false pretenses, or content that targets a private individual. Claude refuses whether it wrote the page or the person supplied it, and whatever purpose is claimed, such as a prop or a test, when the page would work as the real thing. If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_version
tools.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. Some clients may publish only to your own artifacts: there the call is refused as owner-only. Republishing is read-then-send: base_version must name the live version you are replacing (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result) — if it is no longer live, the publish is rejected with a conflict; re-read and retry from the current state. On success the new version goes live immediately. When republishing, the artifact's stored connectors manifest carries forward unchanged, and so do title, favicon, icon and contract when omitted. Content is capped at 16 MiB.

schema.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_version
schema.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. Some clients may publish only to your own artifacts: there the call is refused as owner-only. Republishing is read-then-send: base_version must name the live version you are replacing (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result) — if it is no longer live, the publish is rejected with a conflict; re-read and retry from the current state. On success the new version goes live immediately. When republishing, the artifact's stored connectors manifest carries forward unchanged, and so do title, favicon, icon and contract when omitted. Content is capped at 16 MiB.

artifact_title.description: The artifact's current title, as get_artifact gives it. Needed when shared_live is 'public'.

base_version.description: Required when slug is given: the version id this publish replaces — echo the version get_artifact or read_artifact returned (or your last publish result's). Rejected with a conflict if it no longer names the live version, so concurrent edits are never silently overwritten. Omit when creating.

content.description: The complete HTML document, at most 16 MiB. Must sniff as text/html — begin it with <!DOCTYPE html>.

contract.description: Optional runtime-contract version (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Leave it out to keep the current one. Pass one only when the user asks for a different version, or this server's answer says to. # Meshy AI — Workflow Guide

Every create tool returns {task_id, status}, except meshy_creative_lab, which waits and returns the finished model. Wait for it with meshy_get_task_status (task_type is inferred when omitted), then meshy_download_model.
Earlier results: meshy_list_models lists finished 3D models (image-to-3d by default; task_types widens it); meshy_list_tasks lists tasks of any status (default: text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-image, image-to-image; task_types widens it, so an empty default list does not mean there are no printing, rigging or Creative Lab tasks).

## Rule 1: Cost Confirmation
Before calling ANY tool that costs credits, ask which ai_model to use where there is a choice (prefer an explicit one), present the cost and wait for user confirmation.

| Tool | Credits |
|------|---------|
| meshy_text_to_3d (preview, mesh only) | 20 (meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6), 5 (meshy-6-lite, meshy-t2, meshy-t2.5) |
| meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d | table below |
| meshy_text_to_3d_refine / meshy_retexture | 10 (15 with texture_resolution "8k") |
| meshy_remesh / meshy_rig (incl. walking + running) / meshy_uv_unwrap | 5 |
| meshy_animate | 3 per action |
| meshy_text_to_motion | 10 (prime) / 3 (swift) |
| meshy_repair_printability / meshy_process_multicolor / meshy_auto_split | 10 |
| meshy_convert / meshy_resize | 1 |
| meshy_creative_lab | 36; keycap 62; fidget-collapsible 6 |
| meshy_text_to_image / meshy_image_to_image | nano-banana 3, nano-banana-2 6, nano-banana-2-lite 3, nano-banana-2-1 4, nano-banana-pro 9; GPT Image models (gpt-image-2, gpt-image-2-5-flare, gpt-image-2-5-sunburst) 9 text / 12 image |
| analyze printability, balance, usage, animation library, status, list, download | free |

| image / multi-image ai_model | mesh only | + 2K/4K texture | + 8K texture |
|---|---|---|---|
| meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6 (and deprecated meshy-7) | 20 | 30 | 35 |
| meshy-6-lite | 5 | 15 | — (2K only) |
| meshy-t2 / meshy-t2.5 (single-image Smart Topology) | 5 | 15 | 20 |

Ultra geometry (geometry_resolution "2k"/"4k") adds 5 on meshy-7.1 / latest. Confirm the 8K and Ultra surcharges explicitly.
Prices match https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/pricing as of 2026-10-12; point the user there if a number looks off.

## Rule 2: Never Re-create a Task You Are Unsure About
If a create call fails with a timeout, network error or 5xx, the task may still have been created and charged. Check meshy_list_tasks (task_type = that task's type) for it before calling the create tool again. A wait that times out leaves the task running: poll the same task_id again.

## Rule 3: Determine Output Format BEFORE Generating
target_formats is fixed at creation time (3mf only when listed), so ask about the intended use first.

## Rule 4: Identify the Use Case, Then Confirm with User
Determine which scenario below best matches, present a suggested plan to the user, and confirm before executing. When a request spans several scenarios (e.g. A then L), combine their steps and confirm the combined plan.

---

## Scenario A: 3D Printing (white model)
Trigger: user mentions print, slicer, figurine, miniature, statue, physical model — single-color.
Suggested flow:
1. Detect installed slicers (meshy_send_to_slicer, slicer_type:"auto") — present list, save for later
2. Generate an untextured model with target_formats:["obj"]: meshy_text_to_3d (preview), or meshy_image_to_3d with should_texture:false
3. Wait for completion
4. Optionally check printability (meshy_analyze_printability, free). If it reports errors, either repair with model_url = the generation task's OBJ URL (model_urls.obj) so the result stays OBJ — on that route pass printer_type and intended_print_longest_side_mm, since intended_print_height_mm only works with task / GLB input — or repair by the analyze task, then meshy_convert the repaired GLB to obj (1 credit). print_ready only fixes OBJ
5. Download the OBJ (the repair task's, if repaired) with print_ready=true and print_height_mm (local Z-up fix and scaling)

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.
- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

# Re-review rulings — 2026-10-27 (delegated: the user said "just use best judgment")

Marker for every edit that applies one of these: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling Rn)*.
In-text record where a decision is stated: "Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling Rn (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): ..."
These rulings never reverse a prior user ruling; they settle consequences the user's rulings left ambiguous or unimplementable.

## General rules (G)
- G1 Owner wins: where two GDDs disagree on a value, field, unit or contract, the registry `source:` GDD wins and the other conforms. If the thing is unregistered, the PUBLISHER of the field/signal/value wins and the consumer conforms.
- G2 Specialist disagreements: follow the creative-director's stated resolution in that GDD's disagreements list. Where the CD said "the user should choose", take the CD's stated lean.
- G3 Carried-over blockers (flagged "still not fixed"/"carried over"): previous edits did not land. After each edit, Grep for the old wording and confirm it is gone everywhere in the GDD (body, examples, ACs, tuning tables, OQs).
- G4 ACs that contradict the GDD's own formulas: recompute from the formula at registry defaults; never weaken a formula to match an AC.
- G5 Division/overflow at boundaries: guard explicitly (e.g. avail == 0 -> share 0, everything unserved); state the guard in the formula and add a boundary AC.

## Cross-cutting rulings (R)
- R1 Restore epoch (consequence of X8/D16). Save/Load OWNS `restore_epoch` as a persisted integer in the save slot header (u32, starts 0). On every restore (death restart or load), Save/Load increments it and durably writes the header (atomic header-only write) BEFORE the first RUNNING tick, so reloading the same autosave twice, in-process or after a fresh process start, gives a new epoch each time. The kernel exposes it read-only in `kernel.clock` as (T, world_seed, restore_epoch) — sim-visible, pure. The KERNEL (command-simulation-layer.md) owns the one derivation for threat draws, counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE x restore_epoch, and owns RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE (value 1048576 unchanged; registry_request: move its source from attention-system.md to command-simulation-layer.md, with attention, horror and save-load in referenced_by). The stream name hash stays cached and unchanged. Attention and Horror call the kernel derivation; neither defines its own. Graph physical failures and persisted counters never read the epoch. Determinism (G3/G4) is defined given (save bytes, restore_epoch): the same pair replays identically; tests pin the epoch. Required ACs: (i) two successive restores of the same save yield epochs e and e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) a fresh-process reload of the same slot also advances the epoch; (iii) same (save, epoch) pair -> identical draws. Save/Load's 'none of it able to alter the sim' is amended to exempt restore_epoch.
- R2 seq (kernel CR-4). The kernel stamps `seq` internally per (peer, source); callers never choose it; `submit()` stays void (fire-and-forget). A caller may attach an opaque `correlation` field (int) that the kernel echoes unchanged in the result/rejection event. Player Controller keys pre-play tokens by `correlation`. Update the kernel seq ACs (L883, L892, L902-904) and PC-7 together.
- R3 Completion sentinel (kernel CR-19b). Every owner callable receives `ctx`; results flow through ctx, never the return value: validate reports via ctx.ok() / ctx.reject(reason); snapshot via ctx.put(payload); apply(cmd, write_scope, ctx). Every callable's only return is `return ctx.complete()` (a typed token). No `-> void` owner callables.
- R4 Mouse aim. The Player Controller's form is canonical: cursor_aim_world = f_q + (cursor_vp - picture_centre) / k_eff, where f_q is the quantized camera position actually used for the frame. The Pipeline PUBLISHES f_q. Aim direction = cursor_aim_world - AIM_ORIGIN, with AIM_ORIGIN = floor(pos) + (0, AIM_ORIGIN_Y) (ruling D10); remove the chest-based subtraction from the Pipeline's D.14b/D.7. Cursor units: the fixer must VERIFY the unit of the cursor source (e.g. Viewport.get_mouse_position() under the Pipeline's canvas_items stretch wiring (ii)) against docs/engine-reference/godot/ and the Pipeline's own wiring text, then make the label, the variable table and the divisor agree in both GDDs; if the reference cannot settle it, mark the unit claim [UNV] and add an in-engine verification AC.
- R5 Carry tell (consequence of X3). Owners: Attention owns the intake numbers and the ONE integrator (Attention's walk-in convention and tick accounting are canonical; Boarding quotes them); Boarding owns the live-choice acceptance (AC-BS-123) and its K definitions, stated with Attention's integrator; Derelict owns the route length (21-28 tiles, X3). Scope: the burden applies only to SALVAGE carry — an item carried that was picked up inside a non-home locus (derelict) — moving or standing, until dropped/installed/thrown; never to carrying at home or of the player's own kit. Pace-robustness, scoped to that salvage carry only: (a) while a salvage carry is held, attention decay is suspended (freezing with cargo is priced, per X3); (b) dropping and re-taking the same item grants no fresh TELL_REARM immunity (the rearm timer keys on the item, not the pickup). Attention may re-derive weights/theta within these scoped rules, but must NOT invent weights to force K3-K5 green: all values stay PLACEHOLDER, and if the live-choice margin cannot be shown on paper with honest numbers, AC-BS-123(d) is re-written as a spike gate (owner, the boarding spike, its pass line), which is the expected outcome.
- R6 Pod statuses (consequence of user ruling D60 "statuses run in the pod"). Suit's reading stands: the reserve drains, the cell drains while lit, source RESERVE. Web Map conforms: delete WM-17b's HOLD reading and close ASK-S2. Pillar-2 mitigation: the valve click plays only on the source TRANSITION edge (once when breath_src becomes RESERVE), never per run. Recompute every pod-leg figure from the registry's own leg formula at registry defaults (ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS default 45, not 180; the registry's formulas use 945 ticks per leg — verify in the registry before using) and state run counts with an explicit floor and a carried remainder so every "exactly N" oracle is an integer.
- R7 PD1 static spill bound (user ruling D31: 'static authored spill <= 24 px'). The bound stays 24 px — it is the user's number. The home ship's spine_corridor (computed 26 px) must be brought within it by Derelict Authoring (light placement, fixture position or corridor dressing — the least invasive change; show the recomputed s <= 24). Lighting's AC-LO-69 stays per-push BLOCKING.
- R8 Units of a request field shared by producer and consumer (e.g. Perception LEVEL vs Audio): G1 — the producer defines the unit; the consumer converts. State the unit in both GDDs with the conversion.
- R9 Undesigned dependencies (VS/Alpha systems with no GDD): not a blocker; keep them listed as "undesigned — provisional contract" with the interface this GDD assumes.
- R10 Pending-confirmation defaults and PLACEHOLDER values are not changed by these rulings unless a blocker shows them internally inconsistent.

A blocker that needs a sibling GDD to change is fixed IN the sibling. Owner wins (G1): the registry `source:` GDD, else the publisher of the field/signal, keeps its value; the other conforms. Each file has exactly one writer per pass; requests to another file go to that file's writer.

- **RM-DESKTOP (minimum-spec desktop):** Windows 10/11 64-bit; 6-core/6-thread CPU of the Intel Core i5-9400F / AMD Ryzen 5 2600 class; 8 GB RAM; GPU of the NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti 4 GB / AMD Radeon RX 570 4 GB class (Vulkan 1.2+); SATA SSD; 1920x1080 at 60 Hz. ## R13 OQ-50: Continue of a Save & Quit keeps the epoch (amends R1)
User ruling D16 ("not steerable by quit") outranks delegated R1. A **death-stub restore** advances `restore_epoch` (durably, R14). A **Continue** that restores a `QUIT` generation which is the newest non-demoted verified generation **carries the epoch unchanged** (no epoch write). A Continue of any other generation (after a kill, crash or fallback) advances it. ACs: (i) death restore -> e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) Save & Quit, Continue -> same epoch, identical draws; (iii) kill, Continue of an AUTO/EVENT generation -> e+1; (iv) same (save, epoch) -> identical draws.

## R14 Where the epoch lives and when it is durable (fixes kernel CR-15 vs SL-23 and the REBASED-key/trailer-SHA defect)
- `restore_epoch` is stored in a **per-slot side file** `slot_epoch.bin` (u32 + CRC32), written atomically (temp file + rename) by the Save/Load worker. It is **not** in any generation file, so generation bytes and every trailer SHA and every key derived from them never change.
- When an advance is due (R13), Save/Load issues the epoch write in a **pre-restore staging step, before calling `request_restore`**, polls it per frame (never blocks the main thread), and calls `request_restore(gen, restore_epoch)` only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`. The kernel's LOADING stays atomic within one boundary service. Kernel CR-15 is reworded to: "Save/Load's epoch staging step has completed (EPOCH_DURABLE, or a logged SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE with save_status = FAILED)", and the kernel lists the failure-path exposure too.
- If the write fails or exceeds `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (500 ms placeholder), the restore proceeds with the advanced epoch in memory, logs `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` and sets `save_status = FAILED` (the device is failing; saving is impossible anyway). This is a **listed exposure**: a kill before any later successful write may replay that epoch once. The ACs for durability are scoped to the success path; the failure path has its own AC (logged, status FAILED, play continues).
- A missing or corrupt `slot_epoch.bin` reads as `max(epoch recorded in the newest generation's header copy, 0) + 1`. Each generation header also records the epoch at write time (read-only copy, for recovery).

A `QUIT` generation without `VITALS` in its `risky_cause` is exempt from the fairness step-back. Confirmed; drop "USER DECISION".

13	
14	## Summary
15	
16	Save/Load & Versioned Format defines how a campaign of The Synaptic Sea is persisted and restored: a versioned, self-verifying save container (a readable JSON header, binary block payloads and a SHA-256 trailer) written as a rolling ring of autosave generations, the autosave schedule and its fairness gate, Save & Quit, and the MVP death stub that restarts from the last verified autosave. It also owns the PROFILE store that survives a world restore, the load pre-check and its failure classes, and the block-authoring contract every state-owning system must meet. Read it if you design a system that owns persisted state, a death or restart flow, or anything that must survive a quit, a crash or a version bump.
17	
18	> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Core` · Priority: `MVP` · Key deps: `Command & Simulation Layer (designed; hard upstream); Life-Support Graph (designed; block owner, carries S-1), Player Controller & Input (designed; block owner and the death trigger), Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera (designed; consumer of LOADING); Ship Section & Layout Data Model (designed; `layout.state`, the restore_after root); Ship Body & Interior Physics (designed; `body.state`); Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query, Item & Module Database (designed; block owner / header-field provider); Suit & Equipment, Sanity & Hallucination Rules, Attention, Interaction, Modular Ship Assembly, Web Map & Transit, Horror Entities (designed; block owners); Chart Table, HUD & Suit Layer, Debug Overlay (designed; UI and diagnostic consumers)`
19	
20	
21	## Overview
22	
23	Save/Load & Versioned Format is the persistence layer of The Synaptic Sea. In one sentence: it is the host-owned writer, verifier and migrator of the world's saved state, and the owner of what happens when the crew dies in the MVP. The Command & Simulation Layer (the kernel) captures the true simulation as an in-memory snapshot at a tick boundary and can restore one; everything that touches a disk is this system's: the container format and its header, the rolling ring of autosave **generations** (complete, self-verifying files), the rules for when an autosave is written and when it is deferred, the pre-check that judges a file before the kernel is ever touched, the orchestration of format and schema migrations, the per-campaign PROFILE store that a world restore never rolls back, and the **death stub** — on crew death, the game restarts from the last autosave.
24	
25	**How the player meets it.** Almost never, by design. There is no save button, no slot list, no screenshot thumbnail, no "saving" ring, no sound and no death screen. The player meets four things: an autosave they do not perceive, written on a sim-time interval and at moments of consequence (and held back while a crewmate is down, for ten seconds after one gets up, while a suit is in a critical state or a warning the world owes is still open, so a save does not record a moment the game could have warned about) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; **Save & Quit** on the pause panel; **Continue** on the main menu; and, at the worst moment of a run, the death stub — a breath of black and then control again at the weld, the dock or the door where the last autosave stood, in a world that has not forgiven or forgotten anything, with one plain ship-log line naming the record it came from (UI-11) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The cost of a death is the sim time since the last autosave and nothing else. Rare plain-spoken strings (a corrupt record, an incompatible build) are the only text this system ever sources; their final copy belongs to UX.
26	
27	**What the game loses without it.** The index puts it plainly: a no-win-state game that breaks saves on every module change cannot be played long, and versioning is cheapest on day one. Concretely: the kernel's registry contract (every owner registers a versioned `persist` block) would have no host, so the kernel's save-equivalence guarantee (G4) could never be run against a real file; the Graph, the Controller and the Pipeline already point at a death stub that would otherwise be improvised separately by every MVP GDD; the PROFILE scope that carries Pillar 5's "never knowledge" across a world restore would have no store; and a single corrupt file would end a campaign in a game that has no win state to fall back on.
28	
29	**What it deliberately is not.** It registers **zero state blocks and zero step hooks** (SL-17): the ring's bookkeeping must not roll back with the world it describes. No domain system calls it: the consumer rule stands — a system that wants state to persist registers a block with the kernel and never talks to Save/Load directly. It serialises **data models, never scene trees** (kernel H7, H10), and it never reads, derives or stores perception: a save is the true SIM state (Pillar 1), and it restores every persisted counter and seed exactly (kernel G4, D.10) while never varying by perception; whether perception draws replay identically after a restore is Sanity's decision, not Save/Load's (OQ-37, Pillar 4) *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Release verification runs both stages** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: the file stage (trailer and block hashes) and the reproduction compare inside `LOADING` through the kernel's K-4 report (CR-15, SL-12), plus each owner's closed `<BLOCK>_RESTORE_*` reasons; while `REBASE_BLOCKS` is non-empty the compare is REBASED and checks the recorded baseline. In the MVP the "never knowledge" half of Pillar 5 is **mechanism only**: the PROFILE store is specified and tested with a synthetic block, but no PROFILE block ships; the failure contract proper (what is kept, what is lost, the cryo-bay re-wake) is Failure Contract & Re-wake's at Vertical Slice A and replaces the death stub through the same restore path.
30	
31	**MVP slice vs later.** One place to confirm what ships at MVP and what waits.
32	
33	| Area | MVP | Later |
34	|---|---|---|
35	| Autosave triggers *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | Interval + `QUIT` + `NEW_GAME` initial generation + the `EVENT_TRIGGERS` set, stated once here and in Tuning Knobs: weld and cut completion (`ASSEMBLY_WELD`, `ASSEMBLY_CUT`) and module cut (`SALVAGE_CUT` (registered), from `last_salvage_T()`), whose owners' pure reads are designed and registered; shipping them is a user ruling (D17, OQ-44); a RAGGED cut's `ASSEMBLY_CUT` is withheld until the keep-side cut room has vented and its keep-side ports are capped or the port ceiling has passed (D54) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; pod arrival (`POD_ARRIVED`) and berth (`BERTHED`) join when the registry merge fixes their names. An event whose owner read is absent never fires | Further events as their owners land (SL-4, OQ-24); the choice to ship events at all is recorded in OQ-44 |
36	| Manual save | Save & Quit only | Pinned main-menu slot if playtest demands (OQ-18) |
37	| PROFILE store | Mechanism + synthetic block; zero shipped blocks | Knowledge Codex, scars (VS, Alpha) (SL-9) |
38	| Death *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | Death stub: restart from last autosave, plus one plain ship-log line on the first `RUNNING` frame (UI-11, user ruling D15) | Failure Contract & Re-wake (VS-A) (SL-7) |
39	| Co-op | Payload separable; `saveload.request_save` reserved | VS-B (SL-17) |
40	| Compression | None, `codec` 0 | VS-A review (SL-19) |
41	| API | No `save_now`; no `load(generation)` outside dev builds | Revisit with the Chart Table UX spec (SL-21) |
42	
43	**Vocabulary (fixed).** The index and the kernel's Interactions row call the stub "reload last save". This GDD fixes the terms **"restart from the last autosave"**, **"death stub"** and **"generation"**; the older wording is a stale token routed to the consistency check (OQ-14). Ownership boundaries: block shapes and intra-block migrations are the owners'; snapshot mechanics, `state_hash`, restore ordering and `FAULTED` are the kernel's; the re-wake, the lights-out beat and the cryo-bay fiction are Failure Contract & Re-wake's; world construction is Layout's, Web Map's and Authoring's; the menu's look is the Chart Table's.
44	
45	**Design-level only.** Which thread writes the file, which call sequence makes a rename safe on Windows, which hash library computes the file digest and whether payloads are compressed are implementation choices (→ ADR candidates: container format and trailer; atomic write, backup and recovery; hash choice; death-stub handshake). The engine reference holds no file-I/O, serialization or hashing module (its `modules/` folder covers animation, audio, input, navigation, networking, physics, rendering and ui), so every engine behaviour assumed here is tagged **[UNV]** and assigned to the concept's "save round-trip with version" spike. *(Framing: technical infrastructure with a thin but real player surface, selected as the recommended option for a `Core`/`Persistence` system under `autonomous` automation; logged.)*
46	
47	## Player Fantasy
48	
49	*Indirect — the player never experiences a save system; they experience what it guarantees: **trust without a safety net**.*
50	
51	Persistence has no fantasy of its own. The promise comes from Pillar 5 — "losing the home-ship or a crewmate costs ship and body, never knowledge" — and from the user's binding rule for death: "This is like project zomboid, death is a bitch. It happens." The emotion this system must produce is that the player believes, without ever checking, that (1) the ship they welded is still there tomorrow exactly as they left it, (2) a death will cost them the minutes since the last autosave and nothing else, and (3) the game never records a moment it could have warned them about: it will not save while a crewmate is down, for ten seconds after one gets up, while a suit is in a critical state, while a warning the world owes them is still open, while a breach they cut is still venting, or (if Attention publishes it) during a breach phase (SL-5); and if a death follows a restore within ten seconds, the restore steps back past that save, unless it is the player's own Save & Quit made without a critical suit (SL-8, R15) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R15; cross-GDD fix)*. It does **not** promise to refuse every doomed moment: a death that arrives with no tell and gives the player more than ten seconds after the restore is the world's, not the save's (user ruling, OQ-40). They never feel *saved*; they feel *committed*. Death and quitting never buy back more than the minutes since the last autosave. *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
52	
53	> You never see the save. You see a ship you welded together last week, still breathing, still yours. You go one room deeper than is wise because if it kills you, it costs the minutes since the last autosave — not the hull, not the campaign. When you die, there is no screen: a breath of black, and you are standing where the world last stood still, in a world that has not forgiven or forgotten anything, including the room that killed you. The save never lies about the world and never rescues you from a mistake; it only refuses to record a moment it could have warned you about. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
54	
55	**The player never...** (each absence is a rule elsewhere in this document):
56	
57	| The player never... | Because | What they feel instead |
58	|---|---|---|
59	| sees a save happen as an event | capture stays inside the kernel's snapshot budget (`SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS`, cited from the kernel, not restated) and the write is off the critical path (SL-10) | the world runs continuously; the ship "just exists" |
60	| chooses which save to load after a death | the death stub restores the newest verified generation (SL-7, SL-8) | death is consequence, not a menu |

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

13	
14	## Summary
15	
16	Save/Load & Versioned Format defines how a campaign of The Synaptic Sea is persisted and restored: a versioned, self-verifying save container (a readable JSON header, binary block payloads and a SHA-256 trailer) written as a rolling ring of autosave generations, the autosave schedule and its fairness gate, Save & Quit, and the MVP death stub that restarts from the last verified autosave. It also owns the PROFILE store that survives a world restore, the load pre-check and its failure classes, and the block-authoring contract every state-owning system must meet. Read it if you design a system that owns persisted state, a death or restart flow, or anything that must survive a quit, a crash or a version bump.
17	
18	> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Core` · Priority: `MVP` · Key deps: `Command & Simulation Layer (designed; hard upstream); Life-Support Graph (designed; block owner, carries S-1), Player Controller & Input (designed; block owner and the death trigger), Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera (designed; consumer of LOADING); Ship Section & Layout Data Model (designed; `layout.state`, the restore_after root); Ship Body & Interior Physics (designed; `body.state`); Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query, Item & Module Database (designed; block owner / header-field provider); Suit & Equipment, Sanity & Hallucination Rules, Attention, Interaction, Modular Ship Assembly, Web Map & Transit, Horror Entities (designed; block owners); Chart Table, HUD & Suit Layer, Debug Overlay (designed; UI and diagnostic consumers)`
19	
20	
21	## Overview
22	
23	Save/Load & Versioned Format is the persistence layer of The Synaptic Sea. In one sentence: it is the host-owned writer, verifier and migrator of the world's saved state, and the owner of what happens when the crew dies in the MVP. The Command & Simulation Layer (the kernel) captures the true simulation as an in-memory snapshot at a tick boundary and can restore one; everything that touches a disk is this system's: the container format and its header, the rolling ring of autosave **generations** (complete, self-verifying files), the rules for when an autosave is written and when it is deferred, the pre-check that judges a file before the kernel is ever touched, the orchestration of format and schema migrations, the per-campaign PROFILE store that a world restore never rolls back, and the **death stub** — on crew death, the game restarts from the last autosave.
24	
25	**How the player meets it.** Almost never, by design. There is no save button, no slot list, no screenshot thumbnail, no "saving" ring, no sound and no death screen. The player meets four things: an autosave they do not perceive, written on a sim-time interval and at moments of consequence (and held back while a crewmate is down, for ten seconds after one gets up, while a suit is in a critical state or a warning the world owes is still open, so a save does not record a moment the game could have warned about) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; **Save & Quit** on the pause panel; **Continue** on the main menu; and, at the worst moment of a run, the death stub — a breath of black and then control again at the weld, the dock or the door where the last autosave stood, in a world that has not forgiven or forgotten anything, with one plain ship-log line naming the record it came from (UI-11) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The cost of a death is the sim time since the last autosave and nothing else. Rare plain-spoken strings (a corrupt record, an incompatible build) are the only text this system ever sources; their final copy belongs to UX.
26	
27	**What the game loses without it.** The index puts it plainly: a no-win-state game that breaks saves on every module change cannot be played long, and versioning is cheapest on day one. Concretely: the kernel's registry contract (every owner registers a versioned `persist` block) would have no host, so the kernel's save-equivalence guarantee (G4) could never be run against a real file; the Graph, the Controller and the Pipeline already point at a death stub that would otherwise be improvised separately by every MVP GDD; the PROFILE scope that carries Pillar 5's "never knowledge" across a world restore would have no store; and a single corrupt file would end a campaign in a game that has no win state to fall back on.
28	
29	**What it deliberately is not.** It registers **zero state blocks and zero step hooks** (SL-17): the ring's bookkeeping must not roll back with the world it describes. No domain system calls it: the consumer rule stands — a system that wants state to persist registers a block with the kernel and never talks to Save/Load directly. It serialises **data models, never scene trees** (kernel H7, H10), and it never reads, derives or stores perception: a save is the true SIM state (Pillar 1), and it restores every persisted counter and seed exactly (kernel G4, D.10) while never varying by perception; whether perception draws replay identically after a restore is Sanity's decision, not Save/Load's (OQ-37, Pillar 4) *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Release verification runs both stages** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: the file stage (trailer and block hashes) and the reproduction compare inside `LOADING` through the kernel's K-4 report (CR-15, SL-12), plus each owner's closed `<BLOCK>_RESTORE_*` reasons; while `REBASE_BLOCKS` is non-empty the compare is REBASED and checks the recorded baseline. In the MVP the "never knowledge" half of Pillar 5 is **mechanism only**: the PROFILE store is specified and tested with a synthetic block, but no PROFILE block ships; the failure contract proper (what is kept, what is lost, the cryo-bay re-wake) is Failure Contract & Re-wake's at Vertical Slice A and replaces the death stub through the same restore path.
30	
31	**MVP slice vs later.** One place to confirm what ships at MVP and what waits.
32	
33	| Area | MVP | Later |
34	|---|---|---|
35	| Autosave triggers *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | Interval + `QUIT` + `NEW_GAME` initial generation + the `EVENT_TRIGGERS` set, stated once here and in Tuning Knobs: weld and cut completion (`ASSEMBLY_WELD`, `ASSEMBLY_CUT`) and module cut (`SALVAGE_CUT` (registered), from `last_salvage_T()`), whose owners' pure reads are designed and registered; shipping them is a user ruling (D17, OQ-44); a RAGGED cut's `ASSEMBLY_CUT` is withheld until the keep-side cut room has vented and its keep-side ports are capped or the port ceiling has passed (D54) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; pod arrival (`POD_ARRIVED`) and berth (`BERTHED`) join when the registry merge fixes their names. An event whose owner read is absent never fires | Further events as their owners land (SL-4, OQ-24); the choice to ship events at all is recorded in OQ-44 |
36	| Manual save | Save & Quit only | Pinned main-menu slot if playtest demands (OQ-18) |
37	| PROFILE store | Mechanism + synthetic block; zero shipped blocks | Knowledge Codex, scars (VS, Alpha) (SL-9) |
38	| Death *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | Death stub: restart from last autosave, plus one plain ship-log line on the first `RUNNING` frame (UI-11, user ruling D15) | Failure Contract & Re-wake (VS-A) (SL-7) |
39	| Co-op | Payload separable; `saveload.request_save` reserved | VS-B (SL-17) |
40	| Compression | None, `codec` 0 | VS-A review (SL-19) |
41	| API | No `save_now`; no `load(generation)` outside dev builds | Revisit with the Chart Table UX spec (SL-21) |
42	
43	**Vocabulary (fixed).** The index and the kernel's Interactions row call the stub "reload last save". This GDD fixes the terms **"restart from the last autosave"**, **"death stub"** and **"generation"**; the older wording is a stale token routed to the consistency check (OQ-14). Ownership boundaries: block shapes and intra-block migrations are the owners'; snapshot mechanics, `state_hash`, restore ordering and `FAULTED` are the kernel's; the re-wake, the lights-out beat and the cryo-bay fiction are Failure Contract & Re-wake's; world construction is Layout's, Web Map's and Authoring's; the menu's look is the Chart Table's.
44	
45	**Design-level only.** Which thread writes the file, which call sequence makes a rename safe on Windows, which hash library computes the file digest and whether payloads are compressed are implementation choices (→ ADR candidates: container format and trailer; atomic write, backup and recovery; hash choice; death-stub handshake). The engine reference holds no file-I/O, serialization or hashing module (its `modules/` folder covers animation, audio, input, navigation, networking, physics, rendering and ui), so every engine behaviour assumed here is tagged **[UNV]** and assigned to the concept's "save round-trip with version" spike. *(Framing: technical infrastructure with a thin but real player surface, selected as the recommended option for a `Core`/`Persistence` system under `autonomous` automation; logged.)*
46	
47	## Player Fantasy
48	
49	*Indirect — the player never experiences a save system; they experience what it guarantees: **trust without a safety net**.*
50	
51	Persistence has no fantasy of its own. The promise comes from Pillar 5 — "losing the home-ship or a crewmate costs ship and body, never knowledge" — and from the user's binding rule for death: "This is like project zomboid, death is a bitch. It happens." The emotion this system must produce is that the player believes, without ever checking, that (1) the ship they welded is still there tomorrow exactly as they left it, (2) a death will cost them the minutes since the last autosave and nothing else, and (3) the game never records a moment it could have warned them about: it will not save while a crewmate is down, for ten seconds after one gets up, while a suit is in a critical state, while a warning the world owes them is still open, while a breach they cut is still venting, or (if Attention publishes it) during a breach phase (SL-5); and if a death follows a restore within ten seconds, the restore steps back past that save, unless it is the player's own Save & Quit made without a critical suit (SL-8, R15) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R15; cross-GDD fix)*. It does **not** promise to refuse every doomed moment: a death that arrives with no tell and gives the player more than ten seconds after the restore is the world's, not the save's (user ruling, OQ-40). They never feel *saved*; they feel *committed*. # Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

</system-reminder>

135	### Core Rules
136	
137	**Conventions.** Rules are numbered `SL-n` with names; decisions and routed amendments keep their brief ids (D1–D18, S-1, K-1, K-2, K-3, K-4, K-5). Kernel rules are cited by id (CR-8, CR-15, CR-18, H1–H10, D.11, D.12), as are the Graph's (LS-21), the Controller's (PC-17) and the Pipeline's (C5, `TRANSIT_HOLD`). **(provisional — X undesigned/in flight)** marks a name or contract owned by a system whose GDD does not exist or is still being written; it is repeated at every mention, and none of those names is a contract until its owner confirms it. **[UNV]** marks an engine behaviour not verified against Godot 4.7.2 (the engine reference has no file-I/O, serialization or hashing module); every [UNV] is assigned to the concept's "save round-trip with version" spike. "→ ADR candidate" marks an implementation choice deliberately left open. Registry names are used verbatim and never restated differently: `TICK_RATE` 60, `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` 1800 (Controller), `HOST_PEER_ID` 1, `W_MIN_WARNING_S` 10 (Graph), and the formulas `state_hash` (D.12) and `rng_derive` (D.10). **Kernel GDD values (Tuning Knobs / D.11), not registry entries — kernel registry candidates:** `SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS` 16.7 (K:515), `MAX_BLOCKS` 128 (K:722) and the `snapshot_bytes` formula (K:501); they are cited by name and never restated with another value. All durations are integer ticks read from `kernel.clock.T`; wall clock is metadata only (SL-23).
138	
139	**SL-1 — Container and header.** One file holds one **generation** (or, for the PROFILE store, one profile image — SL-9). Layout is the contract:
140	
141	| Offset | Size | Field | Rule |
142	|---|---|---|---|
143	| 0 | 8 | magic | A fixed 7-byte ASCII prefix followed by one byte, the container-layout id (1 for `FORMAT_VERSION` 1). The layout-id byte names the header/payload encoding only; it never locates the trailer (format law below) |
144	| 8 | 4 | `header_len` | Unsigned, little-endian; `0 < header_len ≤ MAX_HEADER_BYTES` and `12 + header_len + 32 ≤ file size`, checked **before any allocation** (a corrupt 4 GiB length is never allocated) |

179	**64-bit rule (S-1).** Every header value that can exceed 2^53 (`T`, `world_seed`, `state_hash`, per-block hashes, `campaign_id`) is an exact-width lowercase hex string (16 characters for 64-bit, 32 for 128-bit), never a JSON number; hex decoding is exact-width — a wrong length, uppercase or non-hex character is a refusal — and the contract is "8 bytes in, 8 bytes out" with no general string-to-int parse. Header numbers that stay numbers (`format_version`, `schema_version`, `generation`, lengths, offsets, counts, `hash_algo`, `codec`, `tick_rate`) arrive as floats from the parser (the Graph GDD's technical-director note, LS-21) and must be integral and below 2^53 before conversion. A `world_seed` ≥ 2^63 would read as a negative signed integer in GDScript [UNV]; it is stored as the hex of its 8 bytes. **File bytes are not canonical:** dictionary iteration is insertion-ordered (kernel D.12), so two saves of identical state can differ byte for byte. State equality is `state_hash` (or the owners' canonical bytes), never file bytes; the file SHA-256 guards *these bytes* against accidental damage; golden saves are immutable artefacts regenerated only deliberately.

181	**SL-2 — Interchange form and trust model (S-1, K OQ 7, D1).** Each block payload is the owner's `snapshot()` dictionary encoded with `var_to_bytes(dict)` (the form that does not encode objects) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (the earlier `allow_objects = false` argument is not a Godot 4 call shape; the object-allowing forms are the separate `var_to_bytes_with_objects` and `bytes_to_var_with_objects`, which are forbidden) [UNV], or the owner's own canonical byte form where it publishes one (the Graph's `canonical_bytes()`, LS-21), as raw bytes inside the container. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: Item DB IDB-16, registry `item_instance_to_array`, G1/G6)* A **value** embedded inside any holder block also takes its owner's published canonical form: an `ItemInstance` inside any block (today `suit.state` and `interaction.state`, and any future holder) is the Item DB's positional six-element array from `to_array()` = `[def_id, count, condition_bp, cap_bp, patched_at_step, charge]`, encoded as part of the block's `var_to_bytes`, and decoded only by `from_array(a, graph_step_no)` (registry `item_instance_to_array`, IDB-15). A Dictionary form of an instance is not an accepted encoding; this closes the open `var_to_bytes(dict)` route IDB-16 names. The reasons are one byte form per instance, a fixed schema and the size budget (the kernel's `canonical_bytes` already sorts dictionary keys, D.12, so this is not a `state_hash` fix). JSON appears **only** in the header. Decoding uses `bytes_to_var(bytes)` only, never `bytes_to_var_with_objects`; the object-allowing decode, `Resource` and `.tres` paths are forbidden outright (a script path can ride inside a resource; the Graph states "never a `Resource` for saves"). This is the answer to the kernel's Open Question 7. A dev-only `dump-save` command renders any block as JSON with 64-bit values as strings; it is diagnostics, never a load path. The kernel text that calls the interchange form "JSON-safe primitives" (CR-8) and its acceptance criterion that round-trips through JSON conflict with S-1 and with 64-bit fields; this GDD does not claim they are already amended — routed amendment **K-3** (OQ-5): the interchange test becomes a `var_to_bytes` round-trip plus a separate JSON-dump assertion that 64-bit values arrive as strings.

183	**SL-3 — Generation ring.** `AUTOSAVE_GENERATIONS` 3 files (safe 2–5), each complete and self-verifying, at ring positions `gen_0.sav … gen_{N−1}.sav`. **Order is the header `generation` number — never the file name, the modification time or `T`** (after a step-back `T` rolls back while generation numbers keep rising; wall clock is untrusted). A new generation's number is `1 + max(generation seen in the ring, in `quarantine/` (read from the file name), among `.demoted` files and in the manifest)`. R11's guarantee — never delete a generation before its successor verified — is kept and strengthened; the sequence is R11's "ADR candidate" and is stated in SL-10.)* To the player the ring is one logical autosave ("Continue"); it exists for corruption fallback and the RISKY rule (SL-8), not for choice, so the MVP API offers **no `load(generation)`** (a dev-build-only call may exist). `campaign.json` is a **hint, never truth**: a rebuildable cache of the ring (order, last write status, `suspect` counters); if missing or corrupt it is rebuilt by scanning generation headers and causes no refusal; the ring's truth is the set of generation headers and file names.

An interval save is never due while the kernel is `PAUSED` (`T` cannot advance). The MVP set is interval + QUIT + initial + the `EVENT_TRIGGERS` set stated once in the MVP table and in Tuning Knobs (`ASSEMBLY_WELD`, `ASSEMBLY_CUT`, `SALVAGE_CUT` (registered) — the label for `last_salvage_T()` — and `POD_ARRIVED` / `BERTHED` once their names merge); an event whose owner read is absent never fires, and further events join as their owners land. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Shipping events at all trades a shorter typical loss against a learnable checkpoint grammar (the bonfire pattern this document rejects): the user confirmed that trade (Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): ship the weld, cut and module-cut event autosaves, D17, OQ-44) and metric M5 (Edge Cases) measures it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* **Manual save is none in the MVP except Save & Quit** from the pause panel: save-anywhere is rejected because it makes every reload a free hallucination oracle (Pillar 4) and erases the cost of death (the user rule). A pinned main-menu-only manual slot is the single playtest fallback and is recorded in OQ-18, never an in-session save. The Chart Table's API (provisional) therefore has no `save_now()` in the MVP; if one ever appears it is marked "(provisional, reserved)" at every mention. The due-computation is Formula `autosave_due` (Formulas).

The earlier idea of accepting the exposure because the `RISKY` step-back bounds it stays withdrawn, because a doomed save is by definition not `RISKY`.

203	**SL-6 — Save & Quit.** From the pause panel: `request_snapshot` while `PAUSED` (`PAUSED → SAVING → PAUSED`, `T` unchanged), write a generation of kind `QUIT`, and `request_shutdown` only after the write verifies (`WRITTEN`). 518	## Formulas
519	
520	All sim-time quantities are **integer ticks** read from `kernel.clock.T` and converted to seconds only in examples, at `TICK_RATE` 60 (registry, cited). Anything hashed or stored in a header is an integer or an exact-width hex string (S-1); a millisecond budget below is a float used only for logging thresholds, is never hashed or replicated, and so is outside the kernel's determinism rule. **Cited, never restated:** `state_hash` (kernel D.12, registry), `rng_derive` (kernel D.10, registry), `snapshot_bytes` and `capture_time_ms` (kernel D.11), `SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS` and `MAX_BLOCKS` (kernel GDD values, not registry entries — kernel registry candidates), `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` (registry, Controller), `W_MIN_WARNING_S` (registry, Graph). Owned constants are named in Tuning Knobs. Ten formulas follow; the first six are the registry candidates of the rulings (R29, with `generation_select` and `save_verification` amended at the stage-5 checkpoint), the last four are derived bounds and encodings the criteria need.
521	
522	### F-1. `autosave_due`
523	
524	The `autosave_due` formula is defined as:
525	
526	`elapsed = T − last_save_T; interval_due = elapsed ≥ AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS; event_due = (pending_events ≠ ∅) AND elapsed ≥ AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS AND NOT (ragged_breach_open() AND ASSEMBLY_CUT ∈ kinds(pending_events)); due = interval_due OR event_due; kind = EVENT if event_due else AUTO` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
527	
528	**Variables:**
529	
530	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
531	|---|---|---|---|---|
532	| `T` | int | 0 … 2^63 − 1 | `kernel.clock` (read at the tick boundary) | Current sim tick |
533	| `last_save_T` | int | 0 … `T` | Save/Load session memory: the capture `T` of the newest durable generation; reset to the restored generation's `T` on every restore | Basis of the loss window; unchanged by a failed write, so a failed save stays due |
534	| `event_pending` | bool | {0, 1} | Owner notifications and pure reads (SL-4): `POD_ARRIVED` (`web_events`), `last_shape_change_T()` (Assembly), Interaction's `last_salvage_T()` (BS-21) — `POD_ARRIVED` provisional until merge; coalesced; cleared when a capture at or after the event's tick is `WRITTEN` | At least one autosave-worthy event (pod-hop arrival, weld or cut completion, dock, section extraction) since the last write. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* `event_pending` is the predicate `pending_events ≠ ∅`, where `pending_events` is a **set of `(kind, tick)` entries**, not one coalesced kind: a later event adds an entry and never overwrites an earlier one, and an entry leaves the set only when a capture at or after its tick is `WRITTEN` |
535	| `event_kind`, `ragged_breach_open()` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | enum, bool | {`ASSEMBLY_WELD`, `ASSEMBLY_CUT`, …}; {0, 1} | Assembly pure reads (`last_shape_change_T()` names the kind, MSA-33; `ragged_breach_open()` is true while a RAGGED cut's keep-side room is still venting (hull hole open, band not VACUUM) or a keep-side port is still uncapped within `RAGGED_WITHHOLD_MAX_TICKS`; registered, source Modular Ship Assembly) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | The ruled withhold (D54): a RAGGED cut's `ASSEMBLY_CUT` is not due while the breach is open; `event_pending` stays latched and the event is taken once the read turns false, until the keep-side cut room has vented (Assembly's read, band VACUUM) and its keep-side ports are capped or the port ceiling has passed. `ASSEMBLY_WELD` and a SEALED cut (no stubs, so the read is false) are never withheld by their own entry. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* While a RAGGED cut's entry is pending and the breach is open, **no entry of any kind** fires a capture, so a cut followed by a weld cannot capture inside the open breach (the weld entry waits with the cut); event order no longer matters |
536	| `AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS` ★ | int | 5 400 … 18 000, default 10 800 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | Tuning Knobs | Interval trigger (3 min) |
537	| `AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS` ★ | int | 900 … 3 600, default 1 800 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | Tuning Knobs | Floor between any two `AUTO`/`EVENT` generations; strictly below the interval |
538	| `elapsed` | int | 0 … unbounded | calculated | Sim ticks since the last durable capture |
539	| `due`, `kind` | bool, enum | {0, 1}; {`AUTO`, `EVENT`} | calculated | Input to F-2; `kind` is stored in the header and `SaveInfo` (an event and the interval due on the same tick produce **one** save, kind `EVENT`) |
540	
541	**Output Range:** boolean `due` plus `kind`. `T < last_save_T` cannot occur after the reset-on-restore rule; if observed, `elapsed := 0`, `last_save_T := T` and `SL_AUTOSAVE_CLOCK_REGRESSION` is logged once. No interval save is ever due while the kernel is `PAUSED` (`T` cannot advance). The `QUIT` kind is a separate path (SL-6, F-2) and never passes through `due`.
542	
543	**Example:** `last_save_T = 432 000` (the anchor moment, Player Fantasy). A weld completes at `T = 437 400`: `elapsed = 5 400 ≥ 1 800`, so `event_due`, `due = 1`, `kind = EVENT`. The next interval save is then due at `437 400 + 10 800 = 448 200`. Latch case: a second event at `T = 438 700` has `elapsed = 1 300 < 1 800`, so `event_pending` stays set and `due` becomes true at `T = 439 200`. **Withhold case** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: a RAGGED cut applies at `T = 440 000` with `last_save_T = 437 400` (the anchor weld's save) and two uncapped stubs in a V 20 keep-side room (Assembly D.9): `elapsed = 440 000 − 437 400 = 2 600 ≥ 1 800` but `ragged_breach_open()` is true, so `event_due = 0` and `event_pending` stays latched. A SEALED cut at the same `T` has no stubs and is due at once *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Cut then weld:** with the RAGGED cut of `T = 440 000` pending and two stubs open, a weld completes at `T = 440 900`; `pending_events = {(ASSEMBLY_CUT, 440 000), (ASSEMBLY_WELD, 440 900)}`, `ragged_breach_open()` is true, so `event_due = 0` at every grid tick until the read turns false at `T = 445 760` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, then one capture fires and clears both entries (AC-SL-146).

A seat-state hard block never expires (a revived crew reopens the gate once the refractory has run out, 600 ticks later); only soft conditions are bounded, by `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS`, and the refractory bounds itself. A tell is active with 700 ticks remaining: `700 ≥ 600`, so `tell_block = 0`; the crew is `WALK`, `breach_phase = CALM`; `fire` at `T = 10 800`, kind `AUTO`, not risky. The same state under `STRICT` is blocked at 10 800, 11 100 and 11 400 and fires at 11 700 when the tell ends. **Graph example** *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*: `W_MIN_STEPS` = 10 × 60 / 6 = 100. A cable descriptor (`subject_kind` EDGE, `cause` ENDOGENOUS, `sev` 1) has `warn_elapsed` = 47 when the interval save falls due at `T = 10 800`: `graph_tell_block = 1`, `graph_tell_remaining = (100 − 47) × 6 = 318` ticks, no fire. At the next retry tick `T = 11 100` the 300 ticks are 50 steps, so `warn_elapsed` = 97 and it is still blocked; at `T = 11 400` it is 147, the window has closed, and the save fires, kind `AUTO`, not risky. A restore from a save taken at 11 400 therefore never lands inside the first 10 s of that tell. **Cap example:** a soft block from 10 800 onward fires at `T = 18 000` (`waited = 7 200`) with `risky = 1`. **Hard example:** the crew goes `DOWNED` at 17 900: at `T = 18 000` the cap has elapsed but `hard_block = 1`, so nothing is written; `DEAD` follows at 19 700 and the stub restores the generation from `last_save_T = 0`. **Backoff example** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a write fails at `T = 18 000` (`fail_n` 1): `next_retry_T = 18 300`; it fails again at 18 300 (`fail_n` 2): `next_retry_T = 18 900`; the sixth consecutive failure waits 4 800 ticks; a `WRITTEN` resets `fail_n` to 0. **Vitals and refractory examples** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: the suit is `CRITICAL` from `T = 10 000`; the interval save falls due at 10 800 with `due_first_T = 10 800`: `vitals_block = 1`, no fire at 10 800, 11 100 and so on, and the cap fires it at `T = 18 000` with `risky = 1`, `risky_cause = {VITALS}`. A seat gets up from `DOWNED` at `T = 17 700`: `last_recover_T = 17 700` and `refractory_block = 1` until 18 300; at the cap tick 18 000 `hard_block = 1` and nothing is written; at the next grid tick 18 300 `T − last_recover_T = 600`, no longer `< 600`, and the save fires (`risky = 1` if a soft input is still true).

692	### F-8. `load_budget`
693	
694	The `load_budget` formula is defined as:
695	
696	`precheck_ms = t_read + t_sha + t_hdr + t_decode + t_walk; loading_ms = Σ_b (t_restore(b) + t_post(b)) + t_verify; t_epoch_wait = 0 when no advance is due (a Continue of the newest QUIT generation, R13), else frame_ms × ceil(min(t_epoch, RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS) / frame_ms), frame_ms = 1000 / TICK_RATE = 16.7 (one poll frame at 60 fps); restart_ms = LOAD_ATTEMPTS × precheck_ms + t_epoch_wait + max(loading_ms, t_hold_pad); require restart_ms ≤ LOADING_TARGET_MS; hot-path hitch = the main-thread part of precheck_ms, checked against DEAD_TICK_HITCH_MS` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R14: the epoch write precedes `LOADING`, serially)*

698	**Variables:**
699	
700	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
701	|---|---|---|---|---|
702	| `t_read` | float ms | 1 … 100 [UNV]; 0 on the hot-copy path (SL-11) | disk | Read one candidate file |
703	| `t_sha` | float ms | 0.3 … 2 [UNV] | native hashing | Trailer SHA-256 and the per-block hashes |
704	| `t_hdr`, `t_decode`, `t_walk` | float ms | 0.1 … 1; 1 … 10; 2 … 30 (about 10 … 30 over the 30 000 … 60 000 nodes of a Graph-sized payload) [UNV] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | Save/Load, main thread | Header parse, payload decode with objects disallowed, the bounded type walk (SL-2) |

706	| `t_verify` | float ms | 1.5 (D.11 example) … 20+ [UNV] | kernel D.12 | The reproduction compare inside `LOADING`, the kernel's K-4 report, in every build (SL-12) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* |

724	
725	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
